name: Boater hat

card.summary: A flat-crowned stiff straw hat that adds a vintage summer-formal look.

quick.overview:
The boater is a stiff straw hat with a flat crown and flat brim, usually trimmed with a ribbon band. It suits a vintage, summer-formal or theatrical look.

It is worn for style and sun cover; the effect lasts while worn and it can frame the face or hide a receding hairline.
quick.how: Worn with light summer clothing, blazers and striped shirts, often at sailing, rowing or period events.
quick.risks: No health risks; straw can be fragile and an ill-fitting hat can sit awkwardly.

lead: The boater is a semi-formal straw hat with a flat crown and brim, also called a skimmer or canotier, and popular in the late nineteenth and early twentieth centuries.[1] It is made of stiff sennit straw and usually trimmed with a grosgrain ribbon.[1]
It derives from the straw hat of Venetian gondoliers and took its name from boating.[1] Today it appears at sailing and rowing events, in barbershop music and in some school uniforms.[1]

angle.text: Wearers add a boater to give an outfit a vintage, polished silhouette and shade the face.

paras: The hat was fashionable for men and women; Coco Chanel helped popularize it among women, and wearers included Harold Lloyd and Maurice Chevalier.[1] "Straw Hat Day" marked the start of summer, culminating in the 1922 Straw Hat Riot in New York.[1]

timeline.event: Straw Hat Riot in New York City.[1]
